name: Hyssop
grown_as: Hyssop, a small, nearly evergreen shrubby herb. Drawn blue-flowered, the usual form; pink and white forms exist. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A neat, bushy, upright small shrub 30 to 60 cm high, many straight stems from a woody base, green above and woody below.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite, in pairs, often with small tufts of younger leaves in the joints
leaf.outline: Narrow, lance-shaped to strap-shaped, 1.5 to 4 cm long and 3 to 8 mm wide
leaf.margin: Smooth, no teeth, sometimes slightly rolled under
leaf.surface: Smooth or nearly so, dotted with tiny glands, slightly glossy

flower.form: A two-lipped tube with long stamens sticking well out
flower.petals: Joined; a short notched upper lip and a three-lobed lower lip with a large, notched middle lobe
flower.centre: Four long stamens spreading out beyond the lips
flower.behind: A green or purple-tinged tube-shaped calyx with five teeth
flower.carried: In clusters in the upper leaf joints, together making a dense, upright spike 5 to 15 cm long at the top of each stem, the flowers mostly turned to one side

fruit: Small brown nutlets in the dry calyces.
winter: Nearly evergreen: a twiggy bush with some leaves left; best cut back in spring.

leaf: a narrow lance-shaped leaf with a pointed tip
bloom: in a dense spike, mostly facing one way
young: a small upright bush of straight stems with narrow dark leaves in opposite pairs
crop: a neat bushy shrub of many straight stems clothed in narrow dark green leaves
flower: dense one-sided violet-blue spikes at the top of every stem
narrow leaves running right up to the spikes

look_alikes: Lavender has grey felted leaves and its flower spikes on long bare stalks above the bush. Rosemary has leathery leaves white beneath and flowers in the leaf joints in spring. Winter savory is lower, with white or pale lilac flowers. Anise hyssop (Agastache) has broad toothed leaves.
